options.name: api_host
options.description: The hostname or IP address of the pfSense device.

options.name: api_key
options.description: An API key to use for authentication.

options.name: api_password
options.description: The password to authenticate with the pfSense API.

options.name: api_port
options.description: The port number of the pfSense API.

options.name: api_protocol
options.description: The protocol to use when connecting to the pfSense API.

options.name: api_username
options.description: The username to authenticate with the pfSense API.

options.name: associated_rule_id
options.description: The associated firewall rule mode. Use an empty string to require a separate firewall rule to be created to pass traffic matching this port forward rule. Use `new` to create a new associated firewall rule to pass traffic matching this port forward rule. Use `pass` to automatically pass traffic matching this port forward rule without the need for a firewall rule. Otherwise, you can specify the `associated_rule_id` of an existing firewall rule to associate with this port forward rule.

options.name: descr
options.description: A description for this port forward rule.

options.name: destination
options.description: The destination address this rule applies to. Valid value options are: an existing interface, an IP address, a subnet CIDR, an existing alias, `any`, `(self)`, `l2tp`, `pppoe`. The context of this address can be inverted by prefixing the value with `!`. For interface values, the `:ip` modifier can be appended to the value to use the interface's IP address instead of its entire subnet.

options.name: destination_port
options.description: The destination port this port forward rule applies to. Set to `null` to allow any destination port. Valid options are: a TCP/UDP port number, a TCP/UDP port range separated by `:`, an existing port type firewall alias

options.name: disabled
options.description: Disables this port forward rule.

options.name: interface
options.description: The interface this port forward rule applies to.

options.name: ipprotocol
options.description: The IP protocol this port forward rule should match.

options.name: local_port
options.description: The port on the internal host to forward matching traffic to. In most cases, this must match the `destination_port` value. In the event that the `desintation_port` is a range, this value should be the first value in that range. Valid options are: a TCP/UDP port number, an existing port type firewall alias

options.name: lookup_fields
options.description: The list of fields to use when looking up existing resources. This should be a list of field names that uniquely identify a resource.

options.name: natreflection
options.description: The NAT reflection mode to use for traffic matching this port forward rule. Set to `null` to use the system default.

options.name: nordr
options.description: Disables redirection for traffic matching this rule.

options.name: nosync
options.description: Prevents this port forward rule from being synced to non-primary CARP members.

options.name: protocol
options.description: The IP/transport protocol this port forward rule should match.

options.name: source
options.description: The source address this port forward rule applies to. Valid value options are: an existing interface, an IP address, a subnet CIDR, an existing alias, `any`, `(self)`, `l2tp`, `pppoe`. The context of this address can be inverted by prefixing the value with `!`. For interface values, the `:ip` modifier can be appended to the value to use the interface's IP address instead of its entire subnet.

options.name: source_port
options.description: The source port this port forward rule applies to. Set to `null` to allow any source port. Valid options are: a TCP/UDP port number, a TCP/UDP port range separated by `:`, an existing port type firewall alias

options.name: state
options.description: Whether the resource should be present or absent.

options.name: target
options.description: The IP address or alias of the internal host to forward matching traffic to. Valid value options are: an IP address, an existing alias. For interface values, the `:ip` modifier can be appended to the value to use the interface's IP address instead of its entire subnet.

options.name: validate_certs
options.description: Whether to validate SSL certificates when connecting to the API.
